# WMIP: A Working-Memory-Inspired Programmable Probe of Cumulative State Tracking in Large Language Models

> WMIP is a working-memory-inspired probe of cumulative state tracking in large language models. A program generates the items and their answers, with 3 to 100 updates and final-state, intermediate-state or multi-target queries, and the same items are compared under different output protocols. Earlier versions of the paper were titled "WMF-AM".

Authors: Dengzhe Hou, Lingyu Jiang, Deng Li, Zirui Li, Fangzhou Lin, Kazunori D Yamada. arXiv:2603.27343 (2026).

## Main findings

- Across 18 LLMs, accuracy is 84.9% on single-step arithmetic but 31.7% on core items that need one number after three to seven updates.
- From 50 updates on, no model exceeds 10% accuracy.
- Core accuracy reaches 88.0% under a larger budget with instructions to write steps and put the answer on the last line, mainly because of the instruction change rather than the budget.
- Core accuracy correlates positively with public Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard scores.

## Relevant to work on

- testing working memory or state tracking in language models
- studying how written intermediate steps or output protocols change measured accuracy
- generating fresh, contamination-free test items with program-computed answers
- long sequences of updates within a single prompt
